text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's Interior Ministry and Justice Ministry will launch a joint programme for witness protection in a bid to fight violent crime more effectively, deputy justice minister Lyuben Kornezov said.

-- The VIS-2 insuranse company's executive director Hristo Draganov was released on 500,000 levs bail, police said. Draganov was arrested on October 3 on charges of siphoning some eight billion levs while being a director of another insurance company.
-- Some 74 percent of Bulgarian voters will participate in the first round of presidential elections on October 27, a poll research think-tank said.

-- Eleven companies have so far applied to advise the government on the partial privatisation of the Bulgarian Telecommunication Company, Post and Telecommunication Committee head Lyubomir Kolarov said.
-- The European Parliament decided to extend an emergency loan to Bulgaria to help it cope with a grain shortage, the newspaper said, quoting the Bulgarian national radio.
-- State industrial output fell by 12 percent in September against the same month last year while the private sector, posted a six percent rise, the National Statistics Institute said.

-- The Bulgarian freighter Balkan Star 2, owned by the Sofia private Balkan Machinery Ltd. and sailing under Saint Vincent and Grenadines flag, sank near the Black Sea Cape of Kaliakra north of port of Varna. Eight out of nine member crew were rescued by a the passing Lebanese ship Deny-M. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
